headings.text: Why Most Enterprise AI Deployments Fail — and What Separates the Ones That Succeed
Why do enterprise AI strategies fail so often?
What separates strategies that ship from strategies that do not?
How should organisations measure AI readiness before deploying?
What does a shippable AI strategy actually look like?
Where should a leadership team start this week?

page.text: Cognis Home About Us Services Products Insights Explore Why Cognis The case for working with us Case Studies AI shipped to governed production How We Work Six phases, designed to ship Work With Us Insights · March 18, 2026 Why Most Enterprise AI Deployments Fail — and What Separates the Ones That Succeed Most large AI plans fail before the technology becomes the problem. The organisation has not agreed the business result, prepared its data, named a long-term owner or planned how people will use the system. A useful AI strategy is therefore a delivery plan, not a presentation. By Supreme Oyewumi · Founder & AI Engineer, Cognis Group Why do enterprise AI strategies fail so often? The failure is almost never technical. Models work. Clouds work. The problem is that AI initiatives are launched as isolated technology projects rather than as cross-functional business transformations, and the organisation discovers too late that it lacks the data, governance, and operating discipline production AI actually requires. We see the same five patterns repeat across engagements: No executable use case. "We need an AI strategy" is not a use case. The work should start with a specific, measurable business outcome: reduce claims cycle time, triage inbound tickets in under 60 seconds, forecast demand within 5% error. Only then decide whether AI is the right tool. Data that cannot support the use case. Teams underestimate the gap between "we have data" and "we have data a model can actually learn from." Lineage, labels, access controls, and freshness are all common blockers. No owner past the pilot. Pilots that do not name a long-term product owner die the moment the sponsor rotates. Governance added at the end. EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and Nigeria's NDPA all assume governance is part of the design, not a compliance review at go-live. No change management. The people who have to use the model were not consulted when the model was scoped. They treat it as a threat and route around it. What separates strategies that ship from strategies that do not? Strategies that ship are written backwards from production. The deployment surface is specified first: who uses this, in which workflow, on which data, under which policies. Only then does the team decide the model class, the evaluation harness, and the change management plan. The strategies that do not ship start with the model and hope the rest will follow. They rarely do. A practical test: if you cannot describe the target user's workflow before and after the AI lands, in a single paragraph each, the strategy is not ready. How should organisations measure AI readiness before deploying? An honest readiness assessment answers four questions: Data readiness. Does the data exist, in the right form, with the right access rights, fresh enough to serve the use case? Can we reproduce it twelve months from now? Technical readiness. Are the platforms, MLOps discipline, observability, and security controls in place to run a production model, not just a demo? Workforce readiness. Do the people who will operate or consume the system understand what AI can and cannot do? Is there a literacy baseline we can build on? Governance readiness. Is there a policy framework, a risk register, and an accountable owner? Are we aligned to the regulations that actually bind us (NDPA, EU AI Act, ISO 42001) rather than to generic best-practice talking points? Every dimension that scores low becomes a pre-condition of the roadmap, not an afterthought. What does a shippable AI strategy actually look like? A shippable AI strategy fits on a few pages and answers, in specific language, what the organisation will do in the next 90, 180, and 365 days. It names use cases, owners, data dependencies, measurable outcomes, and exit criteria for pilots. It states the governance regime up front and links each use case to the specific controls it will meet. It does not promise a platform transformation. It promises one or two deployments that pay for themselves and build the internal muscle to do the next five. If you are rewriting the same strategy every six months, you do not have a strategy. You have a wishlist. Where should a leadership team start this week? Three moves, in order: Pick one use case, not ten. It should have a named owner, a measurable outcome, and a user who will actually be on the other end of the model. Run a one-week readiness sprint. Honest data, technical, workforce, and governance scoring. No sandbagging. No vendor theatre. Kill or commit. If the readiness is weak, fix the pre-conditions before writing a model. If it is strong, scope a 90-day path to production with weekly checkpoints. This is how our AI Strategy & Advisory engagements are structured, and it is the fastest way we have found to separate AI ambition from AI theatre. page.text: COGNIS GROUP — BRAND GUIDELINES V1.0 · AUGUST 2026 Cognis GROUP Logo & Identity Guidelines Version 1.0 · August 2026 · Applies to all Cognis Group touchpoints: web, product, print, video, and social. This document defines the Cognis Group mark, its lockups, colors, typography, spacing, motion behavior, and rules of use. Follow it exactly; consistency is what makes a mark a brand. When a situation isn't covered here, choose the simplest option that preserves legibility and contrast. 1 · The mark: the C ring The mark is a C for Cognis drawn as an open loop . The ring is deliberately not closed: cognition is iterative — a cycle of learning, testing, and refining that never claims to be finished. The lime keystone sits in the opening: it is the piece Cognis adds. The client's problem is the open ring; Cognis is the part that completes it. The rigid square meeting the fluid circle also carries the company motto Quod Tango Muto — "what I touch, I transform." 1.1 Construction Drawn on a 48 × 48 unit grid; ring center at (24, 24), outer radius 22, inner radius 12 (ring weight ≈ 10 units). The notch flares outward: the cut spans 32° each side of horizontal at the outer edge and 40° at the inner edge, so the keystone sits in a fitted slot rather than a straight slice. The keystone is a 10 × 10 unit square, optically centered in the notch at the ring's horizontal axis. It is always a sharp square — never rounded. Never redraw, re-proportion, or reconstruct the mark. Use only the supplied SVG/PNG files. 2 · Lockups and when to use each There are three levels of the identity. Use the shortest form the context allows — formality goes up, length goes up. Lockup Use for Never for Cognis GROUP PRIMARY — WITH GROUP Legal and formal contexts: contracts, proposals, letterhead, invoices, website footer, press, certificates, first appearance in a formal document. Sizes where GROUP drops below ~5px tall — the suffix must stay legible or be dropped entirely. Cognis SHORT — WORDMARK ONLY Everyday contexts: site navigation, product UI, decks, social profiles, email headers, merchandise, anywhere the audience already knows the company. Legal documents or first contact with an audience that has never seen the brand. MARK ONLY Avatars, favicons, app icons, watermarks, loading states, pattern elements — contexts that are square, tiny, or where the name appears nearby. As the sole identifier in print or ads until the mark is widely established. 2.1 Orientation variants Horizontal (mark left of wordmark) is the default in all contexts. Stacked (mark above wordmark, centered) only where width is constrained: square social tiles, narrow banners, spine of a document. Gap between mark and wordmark: 0.28 × mark height. Mark height ≈ 1.25 × wordmark cap height. 3 · Color Color Hex Role Ink #0D0D0C Ring and wordmark on light backgrounds; dark surface color. Lime #D6FD70 The keystone — and only the keystone in the mark. Also CTAs and accents in wider brand use. Blue #4D65FF Mono-blue mark variant; secondary accent. Never mixed with lime inside the mark. Paper #EDECE8 Preferred light background. White #FFFFFF Ring and wordmark on dark backgrounds. 3.1 Color rules by background Light backgrounds (white, paper): ink ring + lime keystone. Full color is the default. Dark backgrounds (ink, near-black): white ring + lime keystone. Lime backgrounds : all-ink mono mark — lime-on-lime disappears. Blue or photographic backgrounds : all-white mono mark. On photography, place only over calm, low-detail areas. One-color reproduction (engraving, embossing, fax, stamp): mono-black or mono-white; keystone takes the ring color. Lime never carries the ring, and the keystone is never blue. In any single use of the mark exactly two colors appear at most. 4 · Typography Wordmark: Plus Jakarta Sans SemiBold (600), letter-spacing −0.05 em, with two kerning corrections baked into the artwork: g–n tightened −0.022 em, i–s tightened −0.012 em. Always title case: "Cognis". Never retype the wordmark in running text styling — use the supplied artwork. GROUP suffix: Geist Mono Medium, all caps, letter-spacing +0.52 em, set to the wordmark's left edge, ~27% of the wordmark's point size. It is a fixed part of the primary lockup — never restyle or recolor it independently. Brand text: Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and body; Geist Mono for labels, eyebrow text, and technical annotation. In email, fall back to Arial / Helvetica. 5 · Clearspace & minimum sizes Cognis Clearspace: half the ring diameter on all four sides, measured from the lockup's bounding box. Nothing enters this zone — text, other logos, page edges, busy imagery. Minimum sizes: mark alone 15 px / 5 mm; short lockup 20 px / 7 mm tall; primary lockup 34 px / 12 mm tall (below that GROUP becomes illegible — switch to the short lockup). At 16 px and below use the supplied favicon files, which carry an enlarged keystone for legibility. 6 · Motion The mark has one motion behavior — a reveal: the ring sweeps in with a rotation (~110° with an ease-out), then the keystone snaps into the notch with a slight overshoot. Total duration ~3 seconds. Motion is a moment, not a state: in real use the animation plays once , then the mark holds static. The sample at left loops here only for study; in print it appears as the static mark. Motion plays (once) Motion never plays Website first load — once per session App splash screen and loading states Video intros and outros Presentation title slides Event screens and live-stream bumpers Navigation bars after page load Footers, email signatures, documents Favicons and avatars Anywhere adjacent to body text a user is reading As an infinite loop, anywhere Respect prefers-reduced-motion : show the static mark instantly, no animation. Keep the reveal between 2 and 5 seconds; never add bounce loops, spins, pulses, or particle effects. In video, the reveal may be paired with a single short sound cue (≤ 1 s); the keystone snap is the sync point. 7 · Misuse — never do these ✕ Don't rotate — the notch faces right ✕ Don't close the ring or drop the keystone ✕ Don't recolor the keystone — lime, or the ring color in mono ✕ Don't stretch, squash, or skew ✕ Don't place on gradients or busy imagery ✕ Don't add shadows, outlines, glows, or effects Cognis ✕ Don't retype the wordmark in another font or weight Cognis ✕ Don't recolor the wordmark — ink or white only 8 · Asset index All artwork lives in the logo kit ( assets/logo-kit/ ). SVG is the master format — use it wherever possible; PNGs are for platforms that require raster. File Use cognis-mark-black.svg / -white.svg Full-color mark for light / dark backgrounds. Fivetran and Airbyte are continuous ELT pipelines built for analytics. Migratio is a cutover-grade migration platform built for one-time enterprise system replacements where every record must reconcile and every action must audit. Our AI agents (Schema Mapper, Reconciliation, Naming Library, Exception Triage, Orchestrator) catch the bugs that destroyed projects like SAAQ Quebec ($1.1B) and TSB Bank UK. SAP HANA ships as a GA pack too — because SAP licenses its database driver to the customer, the live HANA connection runs against your own licensed instance and credentials. Fixed annual platform fee plus committed capacity. Three tiers: Starter (₦55M / $35K, one project), Program (₦240M / $150K, five projects), Enterprise (custom, unlimited).
